newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS - Cisco busy after profit jump.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS - Cisco busy after profit jump.

text.p: Several Cisco Systems Inc options were busy Wednesday as investors took advantage of an early decline in the stock to buy calls, traders said.

By 1340 CST (1940 GMT), Cisco shares were down a point at 60-3/4 after recovering from a low of about 60 to climb to 62-1/2. The shares were the most active on the Nasdaq market, with more than 12.59 million changing hands.
Late Tuesday, Cisco, the world's biggest maker of computer networking equipment, said its first quarter earnings from operations rose 77 percent, better than Wall Street expected.

Volatility in the options had risen into the earnings report and declined sharply on Wednesday, traders said. November volatilities fell about five points and December volatilities fell around three points.
"When the stock opened down we had a lot of people coming out buying the November 60's," one trader said. "They were driving the stock up and also selling puts."
The Cisco November 60 call traded 3,985, putting it atop the CBOE's most active calls list.
But with the stock flirting with that 60 strike, the option was down 1-7/16 at 1-1/5.
The November 60 put was also active, with about 3,375 contracts changing hands. It dipped 1/4 to 1-1/8.
Other active Cisco options included the November 65 call and the January 45 call, each of which traded about 3,420 contracts.
Traders said the volume in the January 45 call was Morgan Stanley closing out a position for a customer.
"They've been the only ones trading that," one trader said. "They've been getting out of it the past couple days but today they're being a little more aggressively."
Elsewhere, the Intel Corp November 115 call traded more than 18,470 contracts.
Traders were unsure exactly what all the volume could be attributed to, but noted that most of it crossed in small blocks, the biggest being 3,000 contracts.
Michael Schwartz, managing director at Oppenheimer & Co, said it could have been an investor buying back the options and selling out the stock.
Intel shares were up 4-7/8 at 118-7/8 on turnover of more than 12.8 million shares in late trade. It had reached a new intraday high for the year at 119-3/8.
"Because of the correlation between stock volume and options volume, it's not inconceivable that a good portion of that was from some unwinding stock and options positions," Schwartz said.
Other active Intel options included the November 110 call, the November 120 call and the December 115 and 120 calls.
On the put side, the November 115 was most active, with 2,300 contracts changing hands.
The November 95 put traded 2,115 and the November 110 put traded about 1,300. -Gregory Crawford, 312-408-8750/Email: derivatives@reuters.com
